Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes. If for all <MATH_0002>
there is an open subscheme <MATH_0003> such that
<MATH_0004> is an immersion, then <MATH_0005> is
an immersion.

This statement follows readily from the discussion of closed subschemes
at the end of Schemes, Section <REF_0001>
but we will also give a detailed proof.
Let <MATH_0001> be the closure of <MATH_0002>. Since taking closures
commutes with restricting to opens, we see from the assumption that
<MATH_0003> is open. Hence <MATH_0004> is closed.
Hence <MATH_0005> is an open subscheme of <MATH_0006> and
<MATH_0007> factors as <MATH_0008> followed by the inclusion.
If <MATH_0009> and <MATH_0010> is as in the statement
of the lemma, then <MATH_0011> is an open neighbourhood
of <MATH_0012> such that <MATH_0013> is an immersion
(Lemma <REF_0002>) with closed image.
Hence it is a closed immersion, see
Schemes, Lemma <REF_0003>.
Since being a closed immersion is local on the target
(for example by Lemma <REF_0004>)
we conclude that <MATH_0014> is a closed immersion as desired.
